# Feature: Deep water — sanity check

<!-- Generated by the project-manager tool from pm.yml. Do not edit by hand; the store is the source of truth. -->

## Goal

Sanity-check candidate mechanic #41 (Deep water) from Terrain and Hazards before it is used in real levels. Effect: With a life preserver you cross it at two moves per tile; without one it sends you to your checkpoint. Unique: water that taxes moves instead of simply blocking. Useful: a swimmable route with a real cost, not a wall. Source status in the candidate file is 'revised'; it was revised from human review and is now treated as a trial candidate.

## User Story

**As a** player

**I want** with a life preserver you cross it at two moves per tile; without one it sends you to your checkpoint.

**So that** a swimmable route with a real cost, not a wall.

## High-Level Use Case

The player meets Deep water for the first time in its teaching room (mech-41-deep-water-room). Teaching moment: First room: deep water beyond a life preserver, crossed by a patroller's bank. A player who enters with the preserver but treats it as ordinary floor is still wading on the second move when the patrol arrives and is returned to the checkpoint, which teaches that permission to enter and the cost of crossing are separate facts. The sanity check plays that room, exercises every rule below, and records a replayable session.

## Player-Facing Behavior

- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Dark water
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: Without a life preserver (61) entering it sends you back to your checkpoint with the timer running
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: With one, each deep tile takes two moves: the first wades in place, the second crosses
- Given the teaching room, when the player acts, then: That slowness, plus what current and ice blocks do in it, is the mechanic, not a plain block

## Edge Cases & Rules

- That slowness, plus what current and ice blocks do in it, is the mechanic, not a plain block
- Movement/state stays deterministic: state advances only through the pure step function with recorded t_ms; a recorded session replays to the same end state.
- Restart (R / restart) restores the room to its initial state, including this mechanic.

## UI / Feedback

- The player sees Deep water's effect happen on its tile(s) exactly as the rules above describe; no hidden state.
- Any counter, inventory or HUD impact follows the rules above; if a rule needs a counter it is shown while it matters (see Open Questions).
- Failure in the teaching room returns the player to the room start / checkpoint for an immediate retry.

## Assets & Level Data Needed

- Level JSON: new Test Level mech-41-deep-water-room (rows + legend) implementing the teaching moment above.
- Sprites/defs: reuse existing tiles where the mechanic reuses an existing tile; add a new sprite/tile def only if this mechanic introduces a new tile (confirm in the implement task).
- Source: plans/level-design/candidate-mechanics/terrain-and-hazards.yml mechanic #41.
